new_findings_today.title: Destination TTFB cold again (9/10 cold, median 3139 ms) — this time the post-deploy ISR-reset root cause is CONFIRMED, not inferred
new_findings_today.detail: Today's sample shows 9 of 10 destinations cold on first hit (2692-4359 ms; only ziro-valley fast at 838 ms; median 3139 / max 4359). This mirrors the 07-01 uniform-cold reading that was hypothesized (but could not be proven that day) to be a post-deploy ISR cache reset. Today the missing evidence exists: the Vercel deployment id embedded in the SSR HTML rotated overnight, proving a deploy landed between the 07-02 and 07-03 runs — the same deploy that shipped the quiz routes. Pattern across 4 days: deploy night -> uniform/near-uniform cold (07-01, 07-03); no deploy -> mixed warm pattern (07-02). This upgrades the 07-01/07-02 hypothesis to a confirmed, benign operational signature: deploys reset the destination ISR cache and the first crawler/visitor per page eats a 3-4 s TTFB. Core routes stayed normal (median 882 ms; landing 155 ms) and every URL served 200 — availability unaffected.
